title: M3 daily-use and installation exit criteria are still unmet
detail: The project is a tested engineering alpha, not a completed daily-use release. M3 explicitly requires a documented install/launch path and repeatable tasks on supported configurations; issue #6 still asks for an ordinary non-Nix desktop install and actual daily-use tasks before representative benchmarking. CI containers and scripted fixtures supply useful compatibility evidence, but do not satisfy those missing user-facing checks. The newer extensions arrived before those checks were closed.
recommendation: Make installation and a user-chosen daily-work pilot the next release gate; label M3 partial and M4 exploratory.

title: Takeover is cooperative routing control, not a confidentiality boundary
detail: The README says the agent cannot watch typing and only the user can release control. The worker leaves existing read-only VNC running and permits viewer_start and release before the human-control gate; logs are read directly through core.logs and remain exposed by MCP. All processes share the user's UID and filesystem, and the original agent may retain shell access. Refusing screenshot/input tools is useful, but does not revoke an existing stream, recorder, launched process or same-user caller; no hostile-agent exploit was attempted.
recommendation: Narrow the privacy promise immediately; suspend observation streams and sensitive log delivery during handoff, and choose a real trust boundary before promising secret isolation.

title: Profile deletion drops its lock before deleting the profile
detail: profile_in_use opens and acquires the profile lock only for the duration of the check. delete_profile then removes the directory after that lock has closed, allowing a starting worker to acquire it in the gap. An in-memory probe acquired the same lock at the deletion call, confirming the missing exclusion; concurrent live-session data loss was not exercised.
recommendation: Hold a shared lifecycle lock through deletion/startup, with the lock outside the directory being deleted; add deterministic create/delete contention tests.

title: Accessibility traversal can monopolize the only session worker
detail: Every request runs inline in one serve loop, while AT-SPI performs multiple blocking D-Bus calls per visited node with a two-second timeout per call and no overall traversal deadline. max_nodes limits retained output, not visited unnamed containers, recursion depth or total RPC work; application records bypass the cap entirely. A probe returned three applications with max_nodes=1 and truncated=false. During a slow traversal, takeover, status, destroy and log trimming queue behind it; this availability risk is inferred from code, not measured with a hung application.
recommendation: Bound elapsed time, visited nodes, bytes and depth; detect cycles; keep takeover/cancellation responsive without allowing concurrent mutation of Wayland state.

title: A successful wait does not establish the requested combined postcondition
detail: Window and element predicates are checked sequentially, and the element search covers all applications rather than the matched window. Earlier predicates are not rechecked while waiting for later predicates or screen stability. A probe accepted an Editor window plus a Saved element from an unrelated app; truncated or timed-out tree traversal can also make gone=true incorrectly report absence. This undermines the advertised verified-outcome layer.
recommendation: Scope element queries to the target app/window, evaluate the complete predicate together, and represent incomplete observations as unknown rather than absent.

title: Recent typing failures remain unexplained despite a closed focus issue
detail: Fedora CI 37232451508 timed out verifying Chromium text, and 37243415314 received an empty line where 'one café' was expected. The latter fixture now waits for activated state plus 200 ms and subsequent CI passes, but the log calls its cause likely, not demonstrated; screenshot tokens describe compositor state, not application keyboard readiness. Issue #17 was closed after non-recurrence, explicitly without proving the original root cause. Rapid Calc navigation was similarly worked around with explicit cell selection rather than explained.
recommendation: Track each remaining symptom separately with reproducible diagnostics; require loaded receipt tests and preserve failures instead of treating green reruns as causal proof.

title: The reliable X11 runtime is not the default installation path
detail: Stock wlroots 0.19.3/0.20.2 have reproduced mapping failures, whereas Fedora/Arch CI explicitly selects a patched runtime. The README's Nix shell selects stock labwc; the NixOS repair is described as an override experiment rather than supplied as a reusable package. The portable repair script requires exact development versions and does not target Nix store libraries. A newcomer can follow the main quickstart successfully yet miss the repair required for the tested X11 reliability claim.
recommendation: Provide one pinned, reproducible runtime path for NixOS and one conventional distro, with a doctor command that identifies stock affected versions and confirms the selected library.

title: The handoff overstates evidence that full tools are cheaper
detail: Matched seeds 7/8 show fewer calls with full tools but higher standard-suite costs ($1.624/$1.576 versus $1.495/$1.484), with 39/40 successes for each profile. The fixed full-only seed-9 run costs $1.413, but no contemporaneous basic seed-9 run exists in the committed comparison. Hard-suite call reductions repeat, while the strongest cost claim depends on one post-fix run and changed code. Raw records match the export, so the problem is interpretation rather than invented totals.
recommendation: Say 'fewer calls observed; net cost advantage unconfirmed'; use paired seeds, pinned code/prompts, randomized order and raw cache accounting for any future cost comparison.

title: Screenshot retries return a token even when every layout check fails
detail: screenshot retries three times but has no failure branch after the third mismatch. It returns the final before-token and clears needs_screenshot anyway. The probe forced all six observations to differ and still received a capture marked with the fifth observation. Later input normally rejects a changed layout, but the capture itself is misrepresented and a layout that changes back can pass the token check.
recommendation: Fail the capture or return explicitly unverified metadata after exhausted retries; never clear the post-takeover gate on an unverified capture.

title: Synchronous MCP tools block unrelated requests in the same server
detail: All MCP functions are synchronous; the installed SDK invokes synchronous functions inline from its async dispatcher. desktop_wait can sleep/poll for 120 seconds and desktop_control for 600 seconds, blocking the server event loop across sessions even though waiting occurs outside the worker. A mocked 80 ms desktop_wait delayed an independent heartbeat to 86 ms. This does not imply a separate CLI process is blocked when its worker is otherwise free.
evidence: test: MCP heartbeat probe delayed 0.086 seconds
recommendation: Use asynchronous polling or bounded thread offloading in MCP; test cancellation and concurrent independent sessions, while preserving per-session serialization.

title: Action sequences lack a client lease and can lose their partial result
detail: run_actions is a client-side sequence of separate requests, so multiple clients can interleave steps; the layout token does not detect another client's typing into the same window. Its post-step observe call is outside the error handler. A probe delivered a step then failed that observation and received an exception rather than the advertised completed/stopped record. Retrying an apparently failed non-idempotent sequence could repeat an already delivered action.
recommendation: Add a per-session action-owner lease and cancellation semantics; always report completed and uncertain steps even when re-observation fails.

title: An unaddressed MCP fixture race can fail otherwise healthy CI
detail: Arch CI 37230235686 failed parsing an empty mouse.json after detecting that the file existed. The current producer still uses direct write_text, while the consumer still waits only for existence before parsing. This is strong evidence for a create-before-write fixture race, not proof of a desktop transport failure. No fix or tracking issue for this symptom was found in the inspected log and four issues.
recommendation: Publish fixture results atomically or poll for a complete parseable result; add a controlled delayed-write regression test.

title: Retention is bounded per log file, not per session or installation
detail: Each screenshot creates a retained UUID PNG, stopped manifests remain discoverable, and launched application entries/log files are never evicted. trim_logs limits each file after requests, but neither file count, screenshot bytes, profile bytes nor total state has a quota or prune API. UI identifiers grow to 50,000 and four full RGB frames are retained in RAM. No day-long growth experiment was performed; the unbounded disk paths are verified statically.
recommendation: Add explicit retention limits, disk accounting and a safe prune command that excludes live sessions and named profiles by default; test low-disk handling.

title: Private HOME does not sanitize inherited credentials or host access
detail: The worker copies the full environment and removes selected display/IPC variables; it does not use an environment allowlist, namespaces or filesystem/network restrictions. Other credential or service variables can therefore remain, and launched applications inherit the checkout working directory unless they change it. Profiles are private by filesystem mode, not isolated from other processes of the same UID. These are design boundaries, not a demonstrated sandbox escape; actual secret values were not inspected.
recommendation: Document inherited environment and cwd, offer an explicit environment/cwd policy, and use a container or VM if the user needs hostile-content containment.

title: README omits token-driven coordinate conversion and invites double scaling
detail: The README explains manual image-to-desktop conversion but does not say that passing a cropped/scaled observation token now performs that conversion automatically. Current MCP tool descriptions correctly specify image coordinates with a token and desktop coordinates without one. Following the README formula and passing its token can apply scaling/origin twice and click the wrong position.
recommendation: Document both coordinate modes with a single cropped example, update CLI help, and test README examples against the shared contract.

title: Recycling semantic IDs can silently retarget an old action
detail: short_id clears both maps at 50,000 entries and begins again at n1. A probe showed an old n1 mapping replaced by an unrelated new node. No epoch is attached to node IDs, and observation tokens cover window state rather than the accessibility tree. Long-lived dynamic pages can therefore turn a stale semantic reference into a different valid target; production frequency was not measured.
recommendation: Use generation-qualified IDs and reject references from expired generations; never reuse a live identifier for another node.

title: The JSON response cap conflicts with allowed accessibility output sizes
detail: core.request reads at most 262,144 bytes, while UI requests allow 2,000 nodes with up to 500 text characters each plus metadata. Large legitimate trees can exceed the cap before MCP compacts them. Similar growth affects windows/status; there is no server-side byte budget or pagination. The size conflict is statically established, but a real large application was not exercised.
recommendation: Apply an encoded-byte budget before transmission, expose truncation/cursors and test multibyte text at the protocol boundary.

title: Green CI does not cover every advertised application on every distro
detail: Latest main CI 37244764863 ran 59 tests per job with six skips on Ubuntu and two each on Fedora/Arch. Ubuntu skipped four Chromium flows for sandbox unavailability; all three skipped Qt accessibility and visible mode. The matrix does not install kdialog, so the toolkit test can pass with only GTK subcases. Fedora/Arch evidence is container evidence, not ordinary desktop installation evidence.
recommendation: Publish capability-by-environment test outcomes including skips; require explicit expected-skip lists and add Qt coverage where it is claimed.

title: The wlroots repair has strong narrow evidence but no maintenance exit
detail: The repair is small, checksum-pinned and applied with fuzz=0; CI verifies that copied labwc resolves the private library and repeatedly checks X11 receipt. That is a justified response to a traced failure. However, latest Fedora/Arch images float while the script accepts only exact wlroots 0.19.3/0.20.2 development packages, so routine image upgrades can break builds. No upstream issue/MR or removal criterion is linked in runtime/README.md; upstream acceptance was not independently investigated.
recommendation: Pin a supported runtime matrix, retain the ordering reproducer, track an upstream submission and define when to retire the private patch; keep latest-distro discovery separate from release gates.

title: Benchmark saturation says little about daily-work completion
detail: The standard suite mostly consists of small local pages, dialogs and terminal/editor fixtures; the hard suite adds multi-window tasks but remains short and heavily controlled. Applications are pre-launched with deterministic delays, so provisioning, normal project setup, recovery, user handoff and long sessions are largely absent. Forty successes across two standard runs are correlated repetitions of 20 tasks, not 40 independent real workflows. The original intent explicitly permits shell/API use, while these GUI-restricted trials intentionally measure a narrower mechanism.
recommendation: Keep these as regression fixtures; derive a separate small set of real workflows from user work and measure intervention, wrong actions and end-to-end time.

title: Cua results establish narrow feasibility, not superiority or parity
detail: The retained comparison contains three browser fixtures with two trials each per runtime, matching generated page hashes and successful verifiers. I recomputed 46/49 calls and $0.5183458/$0.529132 totals and checked all 12 page hashes against raw files. Browser versions, Wayland/X11 desktops, screenshot sizes, resource caps, prompt/tool surfaces and cache counters differ; startup is excluded from agent time and native startup was not measured. This restricted adapter comparison is not an evaluation of the full current Cua product.
recommendation: Retain the no-winner conclusion; separate user-experience comparisons of each default product from causal tests of tool design in a matched environment.

title: Benchmark records and exit codes do not enforce reproducible successful runs
detail: benchmark.py always returns zero after recording results, even for failed tasks or cleanup failures; the container harness returns nonzero for errors but not plain verifier failures. Standard summaries do not capture source revision, runtime versions, prompt/schema hashes or CPU limits automatically. Exported tool-profile records drop detailed verification and error fields, although raw artifacts currently exist and match the exported metrics. The documented discarded usage-limit round should remain explicitly accounted for rather than silently disappear from comparisons.
recommendation: Define distinct normal/negative-control exit rules; retain all attempted-run statuses and versioned provenance; export verification/error/cleanup evidence without sensitive transcripts.

title: Login and profile fixtures have not established the real handoff experience
detail: Tests verify local cookie persistence, profile exclusivity, synthetic RFB typing and clipboard clearing. They do not demonstrate a real third-party login, a password-manager/2FA interaction, an agent waiting and resuming correctly, or non-US human keyboard layout handling. The development log explicitly records these gaps. Thus takeover/profiles are implemented mechanisms, not a validated daily login workflow.
recommendation: Have the user choose one low-risk real login and validate the complete handoff/resume flow with scoped authorization; test their actual keyboard layout.

title: Clipboard clearing failure silently hands control back
detail: release catches clipboard-clearing errors, writes only a log warning and returns control to the agent. A probe forced clear_selection to fail and still received owner=agent. This contradicts the unconditional README statement that release clears both selections and may leave an application-owned copied secret available. Normal tested paths do clear it; failure behavior is the gap.
recommendation: Return explicit clipboard-cleared status and keep control paused on failure when secret paste was enabled; require a deliberate user override to continue.

title: Lifecycle ownership still has PID and double-supervisor failure boundaries
detail: Teardown snapshots /proc then signals numeric PIDs, leaving PID-reuse races; if both supervisors die, tokenless escaped processes are undiscoverable by recover. Host-service-launched processes can also fall outside the owned tree. Profile flock ownership sits in the worker, so abnormal worker death releases the lock before guardian cleanup necessarily finishes. Normal and single-worker-crash behavior have repeated test evidence, but these stronger failure combinations are not covered by the same guarantee.
recommendation: Add PID start-time/pidfd validation where available and a profile recovery state; evaluate delegated cgroups or a container for stronger ownership only against the chosen portability requirements.

title: Current documentation mixes historical limitations with implemented behavior
detail: README still says accessibility trees are unimplemented; BENCHMARK still says no baseline comparison has run before presenting one later. START_HERE names only early runtime dependencies and has overlapping, stale priority lists; PROJECT_PLAN calls the runtime packaged while convenient supported-runtime installation remains open. Most CLI command names and arguments match the parser, but stale prose makes the handoff unreliable as a decision document.
recommendation: Separate historical evidence from current status, replace the priority block with the proposed release gates, and validate examples against current CLI/MCP contracts.

title: The small core has become a large protocol and lifecycle maintenance surface
detail: worker.py is 1,156 lines spanning process ownership, environment setup, protocol dispatch, observation, accessibility, VNC, retention and cleanup. The project also maintains a 600-line Wayland wire client and duplicated lifecycle/ownership logic in the historical M0 script. These choices bought concrete input reliability, but widen the review burden and make contract drift easier. Ruff passes; I did not establish arbitrary code as dead merely because it is old.
evidence: test: uv run --no-sync --offline ruff check --no-cache src scripts tests benchmarks passed
recommendation: Extract bounded subsystems only while fixing tested defects; centralize operation schemas and mark historical experiment code clearly, without building a multi-backend framework.

title: The foundational private desktop loop has substantial actual evidence
detail: Explicit session routing, private compositor/D-Bus/HOME, persistent keyboard/pointer devices, foreign-toplevel focus, image capture and owned-process cleanup are implemented and exercised with actual application receipt. Latest CI adds 30 Ubuntu focus/crash/X11 repetitions and 100 loaded X11 repetitions on each repaired Fedora/Arch runtime. Eleven existing non-desktop tests and lint also passed in this review. NixOS host noninterference claims remain historical before/after observations, not continuous proof or a new measurement here.
recommendation: Preserve the working labwc backend and real receipt assertions; prioritize operational gaps instead of restarting M0.

title: Semantic UI is implemented, but its validated surface remains narrow
detail: Private AT-SPI registry startup, filtered tree inspection and press/focus/set_text exist, with a keyboard fallback for Chromium. Tests cover GTK dialogs, Chromium forms and a Qt dialog when dependencies are present; latest CI does not run the Qt case. LibreOffice/Electron semantic coverage and large-tree latency are explicitly unverified. This is meaningful capability, not complete accessibility support.
recommendation: Choose semantic expansion only from recurring pilot failures, after traversal and target-validity fixes.

title: Direction stayed aligned, but implementation breadth outran acceptance evidence
detail: The project remains an environment for existing agents rather than a new agent or a specialized debugging product. Persistent input, private bus, crash recovery and the X11 patch are justified by concrete failures; takeover/profiles follow the original interaction goal. Waiting, sequences, crops and semantic UI implement previously deferred extensions and have useful tests, but their priority over packaging and daily use is not established. prompt2 explicitly presents the portable machine as a possible future direction, so not shipping VMs/Windows/macOS is not a broken first-release promise.
recommendation: Stop feature accumulation until the existing breadth earns repeated use; keep portable-machine work as a separately gated option.

title: wbox overlaps the core promise and offers onboarding ideas to adopt
detail: wbox documents a private/headless compositor, screenshots/input/MCP, per-project configuration, distro installation steps and a clean command. That overlaps the central concept rather than merely an adjacent feature. This project has directly inspectable session/crash/receipt evidence and a conservative no-clipboard-bridge default; that is a local design advantage, not proof that wbox is less reliable. wbox's stronger isolation wording was not verified.
recommendation: Adopt the first-run configuration, dependency diagnosis and housekeeping patterns; compare one real workflow before considering component reuse.

title: kde-mcp provides useful policy and semantic-response design precedents
detail: kde-mcp documents AT-SPI-first control, headless KWin, a mutation lease, policy gates, structured audit records and response diffs. Those are worth studying for ownership and evidence design; its cost-reduction and daily-use claims are not independently verified here. Its KDE-specific integration differs from this project's private labwc backend on a Hyprland host. There is no evidence here for a general performance ranking.
recommendation: Evaluate leases, concise state differences and action audit records; avoid copying host-specific policy machinery without a concrete requirement.

title: Cua already spans much of the portable-machine vision
detail: Cua documents cross-platform drivers, local/container/VM environments, typed SDKs, onboarding and evaluation tooling; Spaces also documents handoff and signed-in environments. This project is smaller and locally controlled, but lacks comparable provisioning and host-platform breadth. Its retained comparison tests one older restricted local-container configuration, not all those capabilities. Component licensing differs, so reuse requires checking the chosen component rather than relying on a repository headline.
recommendation: Before pursuing O4, test whether an existing Cua environment can host this runtime or satisfy the user's workflow; adopt readiness/provenance ideas where useful.

title: E2B offers a provisioned desktop API rather than a local same-user session
detail: E2B Desktop documents sandbox creation, desktop input/screenshots, window APIs and authenticated streaming through Python/JavaScript SDKs. Its hosted quickstart requires an API key; this project's local runtime does not require a desktop-provider account. Provisioning convenience and sandbox isolation are documented advantages to evaluate, while actual isolation, latency, pricing and task reliability were not tested in this review.
recommendation: Use E2B as an isolation/provisioning reference or baseline when remote execution is acceptable, not as evidence that local same-user sessions are equivalent sandboxes.

title: A bounded action trace could explain failures without changing the product goal
detail: Existing artifacts emphasize screenshots, logs and benchmark summaries, while recent input failures still lack a linked request/focus/delivery/outcome chronology. The plan already identifies action timelines as an extension. Playwright's documented trace model is a useful precedent for correlating actions with observations, but browser DOM/network snapshots do not transfer automatically to a Linux desktop. This is a proposed diagnostic aid, not proof of a new product direction or a request to implement general replay.
recommendation: Add opt-in bounded request IDs, timestamps, target/focus state and outcome references while fixing reliability; redact and suppress sensitive takeover data.

title: Plain waits can exceed timeout and succeed for an invalid session
detail: core.wait sleeps seconds before applying its deadline and performs no session request when no predicates/stability are supplied. A probe with an invalid session, a 1 ms timeout and a 20 ms pause returned satisfied=true after 20 ms. Other predicate RPCs can each consume the core's 30-second timeout beyond the wait deadline. The advertised timeout and explicit-session behavior therefore do not hold uniformly.
recommendation: Validate the session for every wait and propagate a single remaining deadline through pauses and RPCs; return timeout consistently.

title: The one-task client harness can leak sessions on timeout
detail: claude_code_task.py launches the external client and parses its transcript before reaching session cleanup, with no encompassing finally. A client timeout, malformed transcript or failed verification request can therefore bypass cleanup after a desktop was created. The normal successful reports do not cover this failure path. No paid or desktop run was performed to trigger it.
recommendation: Wrap all client execution/verification in a scoped cleanup finally and record uncertain leftovers even when transcript processing fails.

title: Observation tokens cannot detect window movement or in-window target changes
detail: Tokens hash output size/scale, window IDs/app IDs/states/parents and control epoch. They contain neither pixels nor window geometry, titles or semantic-tree state; ordinary input may omit a token entirely. Thus a moved/resized window with unchanged states or a replaced in-window button can still accept old coordinates, and a check-to-input race remains. These are documented or statically visible boundaries, not a demonstrated physical-desktop routing failure.
recommendation: Name this a window-topology/focus guard, retain explicit outcome checks and consider target-specific preconditions only where real failures justify them.
